sources.title: Poor writing, not specialized concepts, drives processing difficulty in legal language
sources.authors: Eric Martínez; Frank Mollica; Edward Gibson
sources.population: English legal-text readers; corpus and controlled text comparison
sources.exposure: Contract passages with legalese features versus edited alternatives
sources.result: Editing surface features is separable from changing legal concepts. Benefits differ by feature; passive voice is not equivalent to center embedding.
sources.limitations: Corpus plus experiment; not an estimate for all audiences or all dimensions; no direct cognitive-load measure extracted.

sources.title: The effects of communicating uncertainty on public trust in facts and numbers
sources.authors: Anne Marthe van der Bles; Sander van der Linden; Alexandra L. J. Freeman; David J. Spiegelhalter
sources.population: Five experiments on factual numerical messages
sources.measurement: Trust in numbers and sources; perceived uncertainty
sources.result: Numeric ranges generally produced little source-trust reduction; verbal expressions sometimes reduced trust. Outcome-specific and format-dependent.
sources.limitations: Do not interpret source trust as self-confidence calibration; studies within one research program are not five independent replications.

sources.title: The effects of communicating uncertainty around statistics, on public trust
sources.authors: John Kerr; Anne-Marthe van der Bles; Sarah Dryhurst; Claudia R. Schneider; Vivien Chopurian; Alexandra L. J. Freeman; Sander van der Linden
sources.population: COVID-19 statistics survey experiments; N=10519 and N=2309
sources.exposure: Numeric range or unquantified verbal uncertainty versus no disclosure
sources.measurement: Perceived trustworthiness of number and source
sources.result: Numeric uncertainty had minimal source-trust impact; unquantified verbal statements could reduce number and source trust.
sources.limitations: Present/projected statistics differ; no transferable effect size; preprint and publication represent the same studies.

sources.title: Working memory constraints on the processing of syntactic ambiguity
sources.authors: Maryellen C. MacDonald; Marcel A. Just; Patricia A. Carpenter
sources.measurement: Word-by-word reading times and working-memory differences
sources.result: Additional processing followed ambiguity; capacity-related patterns motivate a bounded processing-demand hypothesis.
sources.limitations: Trait reading span is not current Working Memory Availability; reading time is not a direct occupied-capacity measurement.

sources.title: Underspecification of syntactic ambiguities: Evidence from self-paced reading
sources.authors: Benjamin Swets; Timothy Desmet; Charles Clifton Jr.; Fernanda Ferreira
sources.population: Self-paced sentence readers with different question demands
sources.exposure: Ambiguous versus disambiguated constructions; superficial versus interpretation questions
sources.result: Ambiguity advantage appeared with superficial questions and was attenuated by interpretation demands.
sources.limitations: Contradicts a universal ambiguity-processing-cost claim, not every bounded ambiguity effect; performance proxy is task dependent.

sources.title: Noise-induced differences in the complexity of spoken language
sources.authors: Catherine T. Pham; Elisabeth A. Karuza
sources.venue: Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology; online 2022
sources.exposure: Multi-talker babble versus relative silence with speaker and listener exposed
sources.measurement: Quantity, mean T-unit length, clausal density, pauses
sources.result: Speech quantity decreased; mean T-unit length and clausal density did not show significant condition effects.
sources.limitations: Quantity is not the full complexity construct; remote sound calibration and sensitivity exclusions limit transfer. Nonsignificance is not equivalence.

sources.title: Do Text Simplification Systems Preserve Meaning? A Human Evaluation via Reading Comprehension
sources.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
sources.population: Human evaluations of human and nine automatic simplification systems
sources.result: Even the strongest supervised system left at least 14% of questions unanswerable from simplified text.
sources.limitations: This is information-loss evidence, not proof of a uniform complexity reduction; systems/corpora are not universal.

sources.title: Getting through: communicating complex information
sources.venue: Bank of England Staff Working Paper 1047
sources.population: 1859 UK public respondents; hypothetical central-bank reports
sources.exposure: Random assignment to texts varying conceptual and syntactic complexity
sources.measurement: Understanding and sentiments including trust; CCI and surface indices
sources.locator: Abstract; introduction; sections 4–5; current hosted version
sources.result: Conceptual complexity mattered more than syntactic complexity; syntactic effects were small/null in these materials.
sources.limitations: Working-paper/current hosted revision; CCI is a specific operationalization, not canonical INF-013; threshold not portable.

sources.title: Sleep deprivation and its effects on communication during individual and collaborative tasks
sources.authors: Benjamin C. Holding; Tina Sundelin; Mats Lekander; John Axelsson
sources.exposure: Randomized overnight total deprivation versus 8–9 hours in bed
sources.result: Builder deprivation impaired model-building but instruction-giver deprivation predicted improvement; other reported speech/task measures were unaffected.
sources.limitations: Role-dependent performance is not direct message ambiguity or surface-complexity coding; no recommendation to deprive sleep.

sources.title: To err is human: patient misinterpretations of prescription drug label instructions
sources.authors: Michael S. Wolf; Terry C. Davis; William Shrank; David N. Rapp; Pat F. Bass; Ulla M. Connor; Marla Clayman; Ruth M. Parker
sources.result: Language, complexity, implicit intervals, distractors, familiarity and attention contributed to misinterpretation themes.
sources.limitations: Diagnostic qualitative evidence does not estimate a causal rewrite effect; any instruction revision requires clinical accuracy review.

sources.title: Improving communication of uncertainty in the reports of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change
sources.authors: David V. Budescu; Stephen Broomell; Han-Hui Por
sources.population: Readers assigning probabilities to IPCC 2007 statements
sources.exposure: Probability terms with interpretation guidelines/alternative presentation
sources.measurement: Numerical interpretation of verbal probability phrases
sources.result: Interpretations deviated from guidelines even with access to them; an alternative communication format was evaluated.
sources.limitations: Instrument-specific dispersion is not automatically objective message ambiguity; full methods not accessed.

sources.title: Are Good Texts Always Better? Interactions of Text Coherence, Background Knowledge, and Levels of Understanding in Learning From Text
sources.authors: Danielle S. McNamara; Eileen Kintsch; Nancy Butler Songer; Walter Kintsch
sources.population: Science-text learners differing in prior knowledge
sources.measurement: Learning/understanding rather than RDS independent agency
sources.result: Text coherence and background knowledge interact in learning; this does not establish a PSYWERX pathway.
sources.limitations: Access was limited; recover exact methods before a mediation/moderation assertion; cohesion is derived.

sources.title: A Meta-Analysis Synthesizing the Effects of Three Uncertainty Types in Science Communication
sources.authors: Zhuo Guo; Ke Liu; Meng Chen
sources.result: Uncertainty types differed; credibility and attitude effects were not interchangeable; cultural avoidance/topic/text length were reported moderators.
sources.limitations: Full text restricted; study-level moderator causality not established; includes primary literature and is not independent replication.

sources.title: Social Network Limits Language Complexity
sources.exposure: Network configurations in a generative model
sources.result: Model concerns language-system evolution, not an observed manipulation of a particular message.
sources.limitations: Do not label model inference empirical or equate language-system complexity with INF-077.

retype candidate
Exposure duration is opportunity for processing, not a component that independently changes the message–audience fit score. The legacy mechanism says moderates, but targets an entity.

Retain unchanged pending adjudication; withdraw universal causal reading. Proposed semantics: usable exposure conditions qualify a scoped decoding claim, not INF-001 causing the INF-014 calculation. Exact moderated edge not established; do not mint it.
SRC-425 and SRC-444 are broad risk/choice reviews, not exact temporal-fit evidence.
HEIGHTENED_CAUSAL: align message, audience, timing and fit rule; isolate exposure from score calculation.

Conceptual complexity and surface-language complexity are distinct, yet the legacy definition mixes syntax. INF-014 derives partly from INF-077.
Propose no endpoint substitution. Retain as research-needed until conceptual-only manipulation independent of INF-077 and audience fit is specified.
SRC-425/426 risk-presentation syntheses do not isolate conceptual complexity; SUP-008 provides a narrower comparison but not a fit-score causal effect.
HEIGHTENED_CAUSAL: no same-time formula contribution; specify independent audience response before any retype/new ID.

research needed
Complete information can be unambiguously contradictory; completeness is a requirement-set ratio, not a manipulable cause.
Exact candidate revision: INF-010→INF-012 remains unapproved; hold sign unresolved and require separate message revision with temporally subsequent ambiguity coding.
SRC-425/428 do not directly establish completeness ratio causing ambiguity.

retype candidate
Adding required uncertainty fields may increase completeness by definition, rather than by an independent causal mechanism.

Proposed derivational input qualification: uncertainty disclosure contributes to the PRESENT_INFORMATION parameter only when uncertainty belongs to the declared requirement set. Do not mint an entity for that parameter or automatic edge.
SRC-428 supplies uncertainty taxonomy, not independence from completeness formula.
HEIGHTENED_CAUSAL fails if the target numerator includes the source; no causal propagation plus recalculation.

research needed
Clear incompatible claims are not necessarily ambiguous; contradiction rule and multiple-interpretation rule differ.
Exact candidate revision: no universal positive sign until a claim set, contradiction rule and subsequent ambiguity coding can be distinguished.

REL-INF-041
revision candidate
Processing difficulty can follow temporary ambiguity, but depends on resolution and question demands; occupied capacity is not synonymous with reading time.

Proposed bounded claim: temporary syntactic ambiguity requiring resolution can increase processing demands during English sentence reading; retain INF-012→PSY-057 only if occupied-capacity interpretation is justified. No universal positive functional form.
SRC-496 COM-B and SRC-515 RDoC are not direct evidence. SUP-004 supportive proxy; SUP-005 ambiguity advantage under superficial questions.
STANDARD_CAUSAL: no RDS; keep reading-time proxy limitations, task boundaries and contrary finding.
REL-INF-046
revision candidate
Trust in a number/source is not automatically confidence calibration for one's own judgment.

Proposed scoped revision: disclosure format may change confidence assigned to a specified judgment, but calibration requires joint accuracy/confidence evidence. Keep endpoint choice unresolved; PSY-113 would be a new proposition, not replacement.
SRC-505/515 broad syntheses do not establish exact calibration. SUP-002/003/013 concern credibility, with mixed/null results.
STANDARD_CAUSAL: distinguish trust, confidence, accuracy; no sign or calibration inference.
REL-INF-048
revision candidate
Conventional metaphor need not increase multiple interpretations; mediated-path provenance is not proof of a full pathway.

Propose state-dependent metaphor familiarity/context qualification, contingent on direct ambiguity coding. Preserve current edge and legacyDirectness until adjudication; do not infer a shortcut or pathway.
SRC-498 cultural tightness is not direct metaphor evidence; SRC-505 broad misinformation synthesis insufficient for universal sign.
STANDARD_CAUSAL: direct segment evidence needed; no reachability-as-mediation.
REL-TEC-060
retain but V1 incomplete
Interface granularity can permit disclosure, but implementation capability and actual communicated content differ.
Retain existing proposition unchanged; require realized content and display conditions before V1 execution. No replacement scientific claim.
SRC-512/513 are normative technical frameworks, not controlled display-granularity experiments.
STANDARD_CAUSAL: separate enabling affordance from realized content; no invented dose or lag.

entityFlags.INF-010: Ratio over PRESENT_INFORMATION and DECISION_INFORMATION_REQUIREMENT_SET. No canonical constituent Driver IDs; requirement-set denominator/weights/update window must be declared. Mechanism/indicators reuse ambiguity language: record tension, do not repair. Outgoing REL-INF-007 and incoming REL-INF-008 need heightened review.
entityFlags.INF-011: Claim-set/contradiction-rule derivation. Incompatible clear propositions need not be ambiguous. Same text can inflate score association; no fixed calculation window/version selected. Outgoing REL-INF-009 is a heightened-review flag, not newly created exogenous agency.
entityFlags.INF-012: Definition concerns materially different interpretations of wording/structure; some inherited indicators instead concern unknown probabilities/missing information. Keep linguistic ambiguity separate from uncertainty and omission.
entityFlags.INF-013: Definition includes syntactic depth alongside conceptual interactions, overlapping INF-077. Conceptual-only operationalization unresolved; do not use sentence length/grade level as the construct.
entityFlags.INF-014: FIT inputs INF-077, INF-053, MESSAGE_REPRESENTATION, AUDIENCE_READING_CAPABILITY, AUDIENCE_PRIOR_KNOWLEDGE. Both causal incoming edges need independence checks. Readability is not comprehension performance. Shared language/audience inputs prohibit aggregate plus constituent propagation.
entityFlags.INF-015: Disclosure is information about uncertainty, not uncertainty itself, recipient perception, trust or calibrated confidence. Explicit interval insertion can change the message property without establishing downstream benefits.
entityFlags.INF-077: Multidimensional objective lexical/syntactic/morphological features. Blocked mechanism/modifiability/etc remain null. Research of reversible text edits does not resolve canonical blocked fields. Fewer words alone is not lower complexity.
entityFlags.RDS-0001: CLAIM_RELATION over MESSAGE_ELEMENTS/MESSAGE_ELEMENT_RELATIONS. Missing operational segmentation/weight/normalization/window/version and blocked metadata stay unresolved. Cohesion, coherence and comprehension differ. No incident causal edge; do not invent one.

relationshipCandidates.proposition: Explicit uncertainty disclosure can alter perceived source credibility depending on uncertainty type, numeric versus unquantified verbal format and factual-message context.
relationshipCandidates.mechanism: Recipients may interpret disclosed limits as evidence of transparency or unreliability; direction depends on disclosure form and source/context.
relationshipCandidates.boundary: Numerical factual/scientific communication and surveyed populations only; small/null source-trust changes for numeric intervals; no guaranteed credibility gain or loss, no accuracy-calibration claim.
relationshipCandidates.rationale: Randomized format evidence supports a bounded causal claim, not a universal monotonic effect. Synthesis preserves mixed and null results; meta-analysis is overlapping synthesis, not extra independent replication.

relationshipCandidates.proposition: Specified surface-language features may change occupied cognitive-processing capacity during reading.
relationshipCandidates.mechanism: Syntactic dependency maintenance and lexical retrieval are plausible demand routes, not measured capacity estimates in all sources.
relationshipCandidates.boundary: English legal and economic text tasks; performance/understanding proxies differ from Cognitive Load. No universal scalar direction over INF-077.
relationshipCandidates.rationale: Processing proxies and null/small syntax effects cannot establish a general exact-endpoint effect. Retain as research-needed.

relationshipCandidates.proposition: Ambient task-irrelevant noise may change the surface-language complexity profile of newly produced speech.
relationshipCandidates.mechanism: Production adaptation under distraction; speaker/listener routes not experimentally separated.
relationshipCandidates.boundary: Multi-talker babble in remote picture description, not every ambient-noise exposure; amount of speech is not normalized syntactic complexity.
relationshipCandidates.rationale: Ratio-based measures were nonsignificant despite quantity differences. Full-construct effect remains unresolved, not supported null and not a universal decrease.

relationshipCandidates.proposition: Conceptual complexity of economic messages may change perceived credibility of the central-bank source.
relationshipCandidates.mechanism: Understanding/attention may affect source assessment; mediation not established.
relationshipCandidates.boundary: Hypothetical UK central-bank reports; CCI/source sentiment instruments require exact construct alignment; not all informational messages.
relationshipCandidates.rationale: One working-paper experiment suggests source-sentiment changes; CCI versus INF-013 and sentiment versus PSY-113 alignment still needs review.

actions.name: Content-preserving surface-language revision
actions.description: Edit specified low-frequency terms or embedded clause structures while preserving the intended propositions; compare the changed feature profile to the original.
actions.scope: English legal passages with selected lexical/syntactic features; no assertion that all profile dimensions decrease.
actions.mechanism: Replacement of specified vocabulary and clause structures changes the text's surface-feature profile.
actions.risk: Meaning/legal obligation drift; specialist verification required. Comprehension and full readability are separate outcomes.

actions.name: Attach quantified uncertainty bounds to a numerical claim
actions.description: Add a justified numeric range and its interpretation to a specified estimate; identity does not promise greater trust.
actions.scope: Factual numeric estimates with defensible uncertainty bounds; do not fabricate ranges or imply that precision equals certainty.
actions.mechanism: Adds explicit uncertainty content compared with the same claim lacking the bounds.
actions.risk: Misleading interval coverage or false precision; verify statistical meaning; downstream credibility remains mixed.

actions.name: Concept-focused economic-message rewriting
actions.description: Revise interacting economic concepts in a message, distinct from shortening words or sentences.
actions.scope: Central-bank information materials; preserve decision-relevant content and distinguish CCI from the canonical construct.
actions.mechanism: Proposed reduction/restructuring of interacting concepts; exact reproducible action boundary needs confirmation.
actions.risk: Removing essential propositions can lower completeness; cannot declare benefit from a readability score.

actions.name: Multi-talker babble during message production
actions.description: Exposure of a speaker/listener system to concurrent task-irrelevant speech during new message production.
actions.scope: Videoconferenced picture descriptions; source and target messages distinguished. Noise is external to the focal task, not necessarily random outside the experiment.
actions.mechanism: Distraction and listener-oriented adaptation are competing explanations.
actions.risk: Not a recommended practitioner action; laboratory exposure does not justify inducing harmful noise.

actions.name: Automatic text-simplification rewrite
actions.description: Use an automatic rewriting system to produce a simplified version of a specified document, with separate human fidelity checks.
actions.scope: Evaluated systems/corpora only; system identity and version are effect/implementation scope, not blanket efficacy.
actions.mechanism: Algorithmic lexical/syntactic rewriting may alter surface features; exact dimension and content-preservation gates required.
actions.risk: Omissions/hallucinations/meaning drift; completeness and contradiction are downstream audits, never direct RDS targets.

actions.name: Make instructional timing and referents explicit
actions.description: Replace under-specified wording with explicit referents or permitted timing descriptions without changing the substantive instruction.
actions.scope: Instruction-specific wording; medical instructions require qualified clinical review. Interpretation variance is not automatically content ambiguity.
actions.mechanism: Potentially removes alternative materially different interpretations; needs direct message coding and a controlled contrast.
actions.risk: Over-specification may misstate flexible or clinically required instructions; no clinical recommendation.

actions.name: Overnight sleep loss before message production
actions.description: A sleep-loss exposure preceding a communicative task, not a deliberate practitioner intervention.
actions.scope: Healthy participants after one night of deprivation; speaker versus listener roles separated.
actions.mechanism: Changes in production capacity are hypothesized, not demonstrated message ambiguity coding.
actions.risk: Mixed/role-dependent task results and null speech findings; no recommendation or new BIO-F01 edge.
